newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Today sees the official start to the multinational protection force to Albania, with the first battalion of 120 men set to leave the port of Thessaloniki tonight for Vlore.

--A finance ministry circular foresees fines of up to one million drachmas for mistaken or misleading declarations on the status of taxpayers' real estate holdings. Property that has not been declared may be restricted from sale or any form of transfer for a period of 30 years.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday gave the green light for the management of the state-run casino at Mt Parnes to be tendered to the private sector.

--Employees of the Electricity Company (DEH) yesterday postponed their 48-hour strike scheduled to begin today following agreement on wage increases and a commitment from DEH's administration to purchase offices for the union. However workers at OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, warned of strike action in May over outstanding wage claims.
--The government's positions on changes to the job market - the starting point for discussions between the government, unions and employers - were distributed to social partners yesterday.
--A film screening at the Greek Film Archives turned into a horror film as a fire broke out in the projection room.

--Mikis Theodorakis is reported to be considering performing concerts in Izmir and Tirana, following the warm reception from both Athens and Skopje to his performance in the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia over the weekend.

--The children of late PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou have sued to recover the home left to them by their grandmother and sold by Papandreou to finance the building of his luxury villa.
--Young and old from Albanian villages are crossing the border into Greece to carry sacks of flour being offered by Greek municipalities back to their villages.
--The government's plans for changes to the job market includes 10 points that directly harm the interests of workers.
--There's been a dramatic turn of events in relations between Dimitra Liani and her late husband's children, following an apparently conciliatory meeting over the weekend.
--There are fears for the safety of a young couple that has been missing from their Nafplion homes for 21 days. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
